title: A protocol for simultaneous Ca2+ and morphology imaging of brain endothelial tip cells in larval zebrafish
protocol: Immobilize zebrafish larvae with 1.2% low-melting point agarose in a self-designed 35-mm plastic dish containing a glass coverslip-filled well.
Incubate the larvae with ES (Ethyl 3-aminobenzoate methanesulfonate).
Remove the agarose around the larva’s mouth and tail using a fine-tipped forceps to allow space for larval growth.
Prepare the Nikon FN1 confocal microscope equipped with either a 25× or 40× water-immersion objective lens.
Set up the heating system of the microscope to maintain an incubation temperature of 28°C.
Open the NIS-Elements Viewer imaging software and set parameters for time-lapse imaging.
Use a laser at 488 nm to excite GCaMP5, which is used for detecting Ca2+ activity in ETCs (Endothelial Tip Cells).
Use a laser at 561 nm to excite mCherry, which is used for observing the morphology of ETCs.
Identify ETCs for imaging.
Place the larva-contained dish under the objective lens of the microscope.
Find the field of the brain using bright field.
Perform an XYZ image of the brain vascular network with GCaMP5 and mCherry at a Z-axis resolution of 4 μm to identify CVP located peripherally in the midbrain.
Identify ETCs budding from the CVP and extending into the midbrain with several sub-cellular branches and numerous filopodia.
Move the confocal plane in the Z-axis to the identified ETC for the following imaging process.
Perform time-lapse imaging for the selected ETC for 3 – 6 hours.
Include separated imaging cassettes with a time length of 30 minutes during the imaging process.
At the beginning of each imaging cassette, refresh ES solution in the dish by removing old solution and supplementing fresh solution to maintain the larva in good condition.
Reset the bottom-/up-imaging boundary in the Z-axis to cover the complete morphology of the ETC.
Adjust properties of the 8-bit time-lapse images, including unit of length (micron), pixel width/height, and voxel depth.
Export the image series into a Z-axis projected “tif” file with an 8-bit type.
Choose one image with obvious Ca2+ activity and minimal movement at the X-Y plane as the reference image in the GCaMP5 image series.
Align all images in the analyzed series with the selected reference image along the X-Y plane using the Translation Transformation plugin.
Subtract the background of the analyzed image series.
Draw the region of interest (ROI) manually to outline the morphology of ETC branches, soma, or other sub-cellular structures.
Quantify the gray-scale value of each ROI as F.
Generate R values with the ratio of FGCaMP5/FmCherry.
Plot R values in ascending order.
Calculate the averaged value of the first 100 frames to define R0.
Avoid including R values within Ca2+ transients for R0 calculation.
Calculate ΔR/R0 using the equation (R − R0)/R0.
Calculate the peak magnitude, duration, and number of Ca2+ transients with a self-written MATLAB program.
Generate the final-baseline-subtracted Ca2+ trace and quantify Ca2+ transient properties based on this trace.
Copy the dataset containing time and ΔR/R0 values into an Microsoft Excel data file with the column title of “Time (s)” and “Delta R/R0.”
Run the MATLAB script (Data S2) and select the data file(s) when prompted.
Observe the iteration process displayed by the script.
Verify the final baseline-subtracted Ca2+ trace shown by the script.
Check the quantification data including area, mean amplitude, and number of Ca2+ transients provided by the script.
Confirm the baseline and Ca2+ transients in the baseline-subtracted Ca2+ trace with the original Ca2+ trace before subtraction through graphs plotted from the program.
Adjust the parameters in the script if necessary: baseline smooth window, number of standard deviations for transient threshold, minimal duration to define actual Ca2+ transients.
Manually correct errors caused by artificial Ca2+ transients due to image movement rather than actual ETC activity during quantification.
Remove the calculation for erroneous Ca2+ transients including area, amplitude, and number when necessary.
Generate a MATLAB script for Ca2+ transients fitting.
Model the rise phase of Ca2+ transients as linear.
Model the decay phase of Ca2+ transients as exponential.
Define the threshold as 90% decay of the peak of the fitted Ca2+ transient.
Calculate the length of ETC branches, ETC filopodia, or ETC growing path using ImageJ.
Adjust the property and contrast of the mCherry time-lapse image series.
Export the adjusted image series into a Z-projected “tif” image file with 8-bit type.
Duplicate one single image from the series for tracing at the analyzed time point.
Open the Simple Neurite Tracer plugin.
Define the start (root) and end (tip) positions of the calculated ETC branch, ETC filopodium, or growing ETC.
Save the trace and dataset.
Define retraction or extension of ETC branches as an increase or decrease in length exceeding 2 μm within 60 min.
